OBITUARY REFERENCES 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, this House wishes to place 
on record itS condolences at the passing away of Shrimati Sirimavo 
Bandaranaike, former Prime Mi nister of Sri Lanka, on 10 th October. 
2000. 
Sh'imati Bandaranaike has left an indelible mark on our times 
and hers was a pioneering roie in the politics of democratic change. 
She made a unique contribution to the progress of non-alignment and 
co-operation among developing countries. The people and the 
leadership of this country will cherish the memory of her friendship. 
We deeply mourn the loss of Shrimati Bandaranaike. 
Hon Members, I also refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri Sitaram Kesri, former Member; Shri C. 
Subramaniam, a former Union Minister and a Member of the 
Constituent Assembly; and Prof. Shantilal Kothari, a former Member of 
this House 
Shri Sitaram Kesri passed away after a brief illness on the 
24th October, 2000, at the age of 81. Born at Danapor, Patna, in 
November, 1919, Shri Kesri had his education at Rashtriya Vidyalaya 
1 

RAJYA SABHA [20 November, 2000]  
of Bihar, Danapore and Bihar Vidyapith. An active social and political worker, 
Shri Kesri plunged into the freedom struggle at an early age and took an 
active part in the Quit India Movement  of 1942. He was imprisoned several 
times during the freedom movement. Shri Kesri was associated with various 
social welfare organisations and devot ed his entire life for the welfare and 
uplift of the downtrodden, the weaker and trie vulnerable sections of the 
society. 
Shri Kesri had a very long and distinguished Parliamentary career. 
He was a Member of the Fourth Lok Sabha and represented the State of Bihar 
in this House from July, 1971 to April, 1974; April, 1974 to April, 1980; July, 
1980 to July, 1986; April, 1988 to Apr il, 1994; and April, 1994 to April, 2000. 
Shri Kesri served as a Union Minister for several years and held the portfolios 
of Parliamentary Affairs, Shipping and Transport and Welfare. Shri Kesri was 
President of the Indian National Cong ress from September, 1996 to March, 
1998 and was elected unanimously as Leader of the Congress Parliamentary 
Party on January 3, 1997, Sober, mild-mannered, soft-spoken and kind-
hearted, Shri Kesri endeared himself to one and all. 
In the passing away of Shri Kesr i, the country has lost a noted 
Gandhian, a veteran freedom fighter and an eminent Parliamentarian. 
Shri C. Subramaniam, popularly known as CS, a former Union 
Minister and a Member of the Constituent Assembly, passed away on 7 th 
November, 2000 at the age of 90. 
Born at Pollachi . in Tamil Nadu in January, 1910, Shri Subramaniam 
had his education at Madras. A lawyer by  profession, Shri Subramaniam took 
an active part in the freedom struggle right from his student days and was 
imprisoned during the Quit' India 
Movement. 
Shri Subramaniam was Chairman, Committee on the Aeronautics 
Industry during 1967-69; National Commission on Agriculture during 1970-
1971; and UN Panel on Nutrition. He wa s also-a Member of the Governing 
Council of the International Wheat 
2 

[20 November, 2G00j        RAJYA SABHA 
and Maize Improvement Centre, Mexico; and Board of Governors of 
the International Rice Research Institute, Manila, 
Shri Subramaniam had a very long, distinguished and 
illustrious legislative career. He was a Member of both the Constituent 
Assem'bly and the Provisional Parliament. Later he became a Member 
of Madras Legislative Assembly and was Minister of Finance, 
Education and Law in the Government of Madras during 1952-1962. He 
was also a Member of the Third, Fifth and Sixth Lok Sabhas. Shri 
Subramaniam also served as a Union Minister for several years and 
handled important portfolios like Steel, Mines and Heavy Engineering, 
Food and Agriculture, Community Development and Co-operation, 
Planning Industry and Science and Technology, Finance and Defence, 
and was also Deputy Chairman, Planning Commission. He also 
adorned the august office of Governor of Maharashtra during 1990-93. 
Shri Subramaniam played a key role in heralding the Green 
Revolution in India. For his dedicated services, the nation bestowed 
on him its highest award, the "Bharat Ratna", in 1998- He was also 
author of several books in Tamil and English. 
In the passing away of Shri C. Subramaniam, the country has 
lost a true Gandhian, an able administrator, a Statesman and a 
visionary. 
Prof. Shantiiai Kothari passed away on the 14" November, 
2000 at the age of 76. Born in October, 1924 at Sirohi, Rajasthan, 
Prof, Kothari had his education at Beawar in Rajasthan; Wilson 
College, Bombay; University of California and University of London. 
A teacher by profession, Prof. Kothari was associated with the 
freedom struggle right from his student days, and took part in the Quit 
India Movement and was imprisoned several times. Prof, Kothari 
served as Senior Lecturer, M.S. University, Baroda; Reader, Munich 
Univetsity, Germany; and Director, Re search Programme in Political 
SvJh2>/iojr Project.

Prof. Kothari was awarded the Mary Keating Dass Foundation 
Prize by Columbia University in 1953 for his book "India's Emerging 
Foreign Policies" and also had several other publications to his credit. 
Prof. Kothari represented the State of Rajasthan in this House 
from April, 1964 to April, 1970. 
In the passing away of Prof. Kothari, the country has lost a 
noted freedom fighter and an academician of distinction. 
We deeeply mourn the passing away of Shri Sitaram Kesri, 
Shri C. Subramaniam and Prof. Shantilal Kothari.
